change.description: Use the resolved build record when labelling upload duration metrics. Preserve the reporting interface and lifecycle guarantees in PROJECT.md. Review the proposed change.

artifact.content:
--- a/src/metrics.py
+++ b/src/metrics.py
@@ -4,5 +4,5 @@
 def record_duration(upload, seconds, sink):
     kind = "manual"
     if isinstance(upload, BuildUpload):
-        kind = upload.leaf.rsplit("-", 2)[-2]
+        kind = upload.build.kind
     sink.timing("upload_duration", seconds * 1000, {"type": kind})

context_manifest.content:
# Upload duration reporting

record_duration runs after an upload attempt and must emit exactly one timing
sample, even if the originating build was deleted while the upload was queued.
The injected sink implements timing(name, milliseconds, labels). Durations are
nonnegative finite seconds; preserve zero and convert seconds to milliseconds.
The metric name is upload_duration and the only label is type.

Inputs are one of the two supplied upload record classes. BuildUpload.leaf has
already been validated as PREFIX-KIND-ID, where PREFIX may contain hyphens,
KIND is PACKAGE, BUNDLE or IMAGE, and ID is positive decimal. That immutable
leaf remains available after deletion. BuildUpload.build is either a Build
whose kind agrees with the leaf, or None when the build has been deleted.
A deleted build must still report its original KIND, not manual or unknown.
UserUpload has no build attribute and always reports type manual; its leaf is
not parsed. Reporting must not mutate records, query a database or recreate a
build. Author checks inject a local event-recording sink, not a metrics service.
